title: Identity component, cosets, and the finite component group
statement:
For a closed algebraic subgroup $H\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(V)$,
the identity component $H^\circ$ is a closed, open, normal subgroup.
The connected components are exactly the pairwise disjoint cosets
$hH^\circ$. There are finitely many of them, and multiplication of
cosets makes

$$
\pi_0(H)=H/H^\circ
$$

a finite group.

proof.text:
A finite-type algebraic variety has finitely many irreducible
components ([lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]). Every connected component is a union of irreducible
components: if an irreducible component meets a connected component,
their union is connected, so maximality of the connected component
contains that irreducible component. Hence there are finitely many
connected components. Each is closed, and its complement, being a
finite union of the other closed components, is closed; thus each
component is also open.

The image of the connected space
$H^\circ\times H^\circ$ under multiplication is connected and
contains the identity. By the definition of $H^\circ$ in
[def-wf-algebraic-components], that image lies in $H^\circ$.
The image of $H^\circ$ under inversion is connected and contains
the identity as well, so it too lies in $H^\circ$. Therefore
$H^\circ$ is a subgroup. Conjugation by any $h\in H$ is a
homeomorphism fixing the identity, so it preserves $H^\circ$;
thus this subgroup is normal.

Translation by $h$ is a homeomorphism and carries $H^\circ$
onto a connected open-and-closed subset containing $h$. It is
therefore exactly the connected component of $h$. The components
are consequently the disjoint cosets $hH^\circ$. Normality makes
coset multiplication well defined, and the already proved finiteness
of the component set makes $H/H^\circ$ a finite group.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed
field $L$ of characteristic zero, and let $G^\circ$ be the connected
component of $G$ containing the identity. Then $G$ has finitely many
connected components. The identity component $G^\circ$ is open, closed
and irreducible, and it is a normal subgroup of $G$. The connected
components of $G$ are exactly the pairwise disjoint translates $gG^\circ$
with $g\in G(L)$, and multiplication of cosets makes

$$
\pi_0(G)=G(L)/G^\circ(L)
$$

a finite group.

*Complement.* For a closed algebraic subgroup
$H\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(V)$ and its identity component $H^\circ$ of
[def-wf-algebraic-components], $H^\circ$ is a closed, open, normal
subgroup, the connected components of $H$ are the cosets $hH^\circ$, and
$\pi_0(H)=H/H^\circ$ is a finite group.

proof.text:
Cover $G$ by finitely many affine opens of finite type over $L$. Each has
finitely many irreducible components
([lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]), so $G$ has finitely many
irreducible components. By Cartier's theorem [lem-ag-cartier-reduced],
$G$ is smooth over $L$, so every local ring of $G$ is regular. Applying
[lem-wf-smooth-components-disjoint] on each affine open, we see that two
distinct irreducible components of $G$ do not meet. Hence each
irreducible component is closed and its complement, a finite union of
the other components, is closed as well. The irreducible components are
therefore open, closed and connected, so they are exactly the connected
components of $G$. In particular there are finitely many connected
components, and $G^\circ$ is open, closed and irreducible.

Since $L$ is algebraically closed, a product of connected schemes of
finite type over $L$ is connected. The image of $G^\circ\times_LG^\circ$
under multiplication is therefore connected and contains $1$, so it lies
in $G^\circ$; likewise the image of $G^\circ$ under inversion lies in
$G^\circ$. Hence the open subscheme $G^\circ$ is a subgroup scheme. For
$g\in G(L)$, the conjugation $c_g$ of [def-sc-group-scheme-translate] is
an automorphism of $G$ fixing $1$ ([lem-sc-translation-automorphism]),
so it preserves $G^\circ$; thus $G^\circ$ is normal.

The left translation $L_g$ by $g\in G(L)$ is an isomorphism
([lem-sc-translation-automorphism]). It carries $G^\circ$ onto a
connected open and closed subset containing $g$, which is therefore the
connected component of $g$. Every connected component is a nonempty
closed subset of a scheme of finite type over $L$, so it contains a
closed point, and closed points are $L$-points because $L$ is
algebraically closed ([lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing]). Hence
the connected components are exactly the translates $gG^\circ$, and two
translates are equal or disjoint. Two $L$-points lie in the same
component if and only if they lie in the same coset of $G^\circ(L)$, so
the components correspond to $G(L)/G^\circ(L)$. Normality makes coset
multiplication well defined, and finiteness of the set of components
makes this a finite group.

For the complement, a closed algebraic subgroup
$H\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(V)$ is a reduced group scheme of finite type
over $L$, and its identity component in the sense of
[def-wf-algebraic-components] is the connected component of $1$; the
statement is the special case $G=H$.
